nodes.name: POMs confinement in PC
nodes.procedure: Firstly, the POM clusters (viz. {PMo12}, {PW12}, {SiMo12}, or {SiW12}) are confined by porous carbon (PC) with sub-1-nm pores as isolated 'nano-capturers' via our reported method.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, the POM clusters (viz. {PMo12}, {PW12}, {SiMo12}, or {SiW12}) are confined by porous carbon (PC) with sub-1-nm pores as isolated ''nano-capturers'' via our reported method.19

nodes.name: Pt single atom anchoring
nodes.procedure: Secondly, Pt atoms are introduced to coordinate with POMs@PC by continually stirring with equimolar [PtCl6]2-. Due to the strong Pt–O coordination, each Pt atom is anchored at the O4H site of each confined POM cluster in a distorted pyramidal geometry.
nodes.source_text: Secondly, Pt atoms are introduced to coordinate with POMs by continually stirring with equimolar [PtCl6]2-. Due to the strong Pt–O coordination, each Pt atom is anchored at the O4H site of POMs in a distorted pyramidal geometry.

nodes.procedure: Pt atoms supported on bare PC (Pt1@PC) were also prepared.
nodes.source_text: As a control, Pt atoms supported on bare PC (Pt1@PC) were also prepared (Fig. S1, ESI†).

nodes.name: Pt-POMs on AC control
nodes.procedure: When PC was replaced by commercial activated carbon (AC) with no confinement effect for POMs, Pt nanoparticles were generated (denoted as Pt-POMs/AC).
nodes.source_text: When PC was replaced by commercial activated carbon (AC) with no confinement effect for POMs, Pt nanoparticles were generated (denoted as Pt-POMs/AC).

nodes.description: HER performance of Pt₁@POMs@PC series in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: The HER performance was examined in a three-electrode system in Ar-saturated 0.5 M H₂SO₄ and all potentials were referenced to a reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) with 95% iR correction. The Pt₁@POMs@PC series exhibit small overpotentials of less than 10 mV at a current density of -10 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀)... small Tafel slopes of no more than 20 mV dec⁻¹ [9.76-18.5 mV dec⁻¹]... Pt₁@PW₁₂@PC deliver a TOF of 24.9 s⁻¹ at an overpotential of 0.03 V... exhibit high catalytic HER durability without an obvious decay after a long period of 100 h

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show no nanoparticles formed in Pt₁@POMs@PC catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As expected, no nanoparticles are formed in Pt₁@POMs@PC, as shown in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images and X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. S15–S19, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show no nanoparticles formed in Pt₁@POMs@PC catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows isolated POM clusters of 0.75-0.8 nm and bright Pt sites at corresponding POM islands for Pt₁@PMo₁₂@PC and Pt₁@PW₁₂@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images show that immersing PC in POMs solution produces isolated, homogeneously distributed clusters with average dimensions of 0.75-0.8 nm... After the secondary-confinement of Pt, each bright Pt site is sited at the corresponding POM 'island'...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Pt 4f XPS shows no metallic Pt signals at 71.4 and 74.7 eV; Pt in Pt₁@POMs@PC has higher valence states than Pt₁@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No metallic Pt signals at 71.4 and 74.7 eV are detected in Pt₁@POMs@PC (Fig. 3a). Besides, Pt in Pt₁@POMs@PC presents higher valence states than that in Pt₁@PC...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows higher white line than PtO₂ indicating Pt^η+; EXAFS of Pt₁@PMo₁₂@PC shows Pt–O peak at 1.63 Å with Pt–O₄ tetracoordination; no Pt–Cl bond visible.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt L3-edge in XAFS spectra also reveals a higher white line peak than PtO₂... EXAFS spectra of Pt₁@PMo₁₂@PC display only one main peak at 1.63 Å from Pt–O with tetracoordinated geometry structure (Pt–O₄)...
